sources.title: Forecasting NCAA Basketball Outcomes with Deep Learning: LSTM and Transformer
sources.key_result: LSTM+Brier loss objective 0.1589 Brier (best calibration). Transformer+BCE AUC 0.8473 (best discrimination). LSTM wins on Brier; Transformer wins on AUC.
sources.applicability: HIGH — same domain. Gap: our 0.22019 vs SOTA 0.1589 = 0.039.

sources.title: Uncertainty-Aware ML for NBA Forecasting (MDPI Information 17/1/56)
sources.key_result: LR Brier=0.199, XGBoost Brier=0.202 on NBA 2025-26 data. MC-Dropout LSTM for calibrated uncertainty.
sources.applicability: MEDIUM — our XGBoost 0.223 vs their 0.202 (gap: feature engineering or training scope).

sources.title: March Madness 2026: XGBoost Cauchy Loss + LightGBM Ensemble Stack
sources.key_result: XGBoost Cauchy loss (reg:pseudohubererror) more robust than MSE/Brier for basketball — handles outlier upsets better. LightGBM adds ensemble diversity.
sources.applicability: HIGH — direct transfer. Try xgboost_cauchy as mutation candidate for S13 (stuck at 0.245). Cauchy loss reduces penalty for extreme wrong predictions on upset games.

sources.title: Winning beyond scoring: explainable ML for CBA KPIs (BMC Sports Science 2026)
sources.key_result: SHAP-XGBoost identifies 5 dominant KPIs: assist ratio, eFG%, defensive rebound rate, 3PT attempt rate, free throw rate. Interpretability without accuracy loss.
sources.applicability: MEDIUM — run SHAP on our best S14 model (26f fleet best) to confirm which features dominate. Could guide engine pruning.

sources.title: Gradient Boosting + Probability Clipping for Brier Stability
sources.key_result: Clipping predicted probabilities to [0.025, 0.975] prevents single-game collapse from destroying Brier score. Platt scaling + isotonic regression for post-hoc calibration.
sources.applicability: HIGH — easy 1-line addition to island fitness evaluation. No engine change. Expected: 0.001-0.003 Brier improvement on edge games.
